# Independent passive visibility diagnostic result

The diagnostic is complete and has zero qualification credit. It contradicts a persistent product visibility pause in the sampled headed scene, while preserving a clear scheduling abnormality. It does not identify a product or capture cause.

I independently reconciled the exact probe, driver, packet, canonical reduced input, current source pins, actual Firefox binary, acquisition receipt and original video digest. `visibility-probe-check.json` records those bindings and the raw comparison. The driver deliberately returned FAIL with no acceptance checks, observations or watches; its separate diagnostic binding correctly reports DIAGNOSTIC_COMPLETE. The original video is `fed5b085b9207e52c53969f712bc896731207082b3fceaedade891e32b31b30b`; this note makes no pixel qualification claim from it.

All 21 samples span exactly 20.000 host seconds. Each reports native document visibility `visible`, `hidden: false`, product `.c.paused: false`, loop started, and an actual 325×530 card at (0,0) within the 390×600 viewport. No native visibilitychange event was recorded. The sole weather request is consumed once through native JSON and the admitted malformed amount remains null, as expected before the ordinary retry opportunity.

The distinct last-render timestamps are 551, 1224, 3279, 7287 and 15344 ms, with observed gaps 673, 2055, 4008 and 8057 ms. At the final sample, native performance time is 20745 ms and the last-render age is 5401 ms. These are observed render-summary gaps. They are not a recorded requestAnimationFrame callback trace, so a particular browser timer cannot yet be named as the established cause.

The retained headless reduced receipts provide a discriminating comparison under the same reduced preference and exact source. After aligning `fixture.started` with the native performance origin, the original reduced control's initial-30s render age is 518 ms; the boundary reduced control's initial-30s age is 830 ms and recovered-30s age is 174 ms. Both still have failed original continuous pixels. Their active render summaries do not rescue those failures, but they show that reduced-motion preference and the product's reduced cloud policy are not sufficient by themselves to explain the headed exponential-looking gaps.

The unchanged product loop calls render on changed simulation seconds and schedules another requestAnimationFrame; its reduced branch holds cloud-motion axes rather than imposing exponentially growing render delays. Native visibility and the product's paused class do not supply an OS-window/compositor or refresh-driver state receipt. An unobserved transient is also not ruled out by one-second class/geometry samples. Thus neither native active painting nor a particular internal throttle has been proved.

The smallest next step is read-only: bind the installed Firefox build to its official refresh scheduling source and identify whether a documented/native throttle path has the observed doubling behavior while document visibility remains visible. Inspect the specific branch and its criterion, not a preference sweep. If such a branch is found, one bounded diagnostic of that exact criterion or a raw native requestAnimationFrame timestamp trace may be justified after its concrete implementation is reviewed. Do not change preferences, foreground state, recorder, readiness or the qualification interval solely from this timing resemblance. No new full qualification acquisition is supported by these data alone.

This diagnostic does not explain the independent headless missing-frame failures. The required outcome remains one readable original reduced-motion interval in the affected Riyadh/current-ingress/night scenario, with genuine preference behavior and intact layout/Moon. Headed scheduling repair, if established, would still need actual original pixel evidence. Firefox default/full scoped acceptance and all retained failures remain unchanged; C16 and pre-delivery C18 remain pending.
